phase3_findings.description: The release note says query_database now gets the rows of every read the agent runs, but with read_only off EXPLAIN, VALUES, SQLite PRAGMA, Postgres INSERT ... RETURNING and tokenizer-rejected reads still get a row count with their rows dropped.
The doc says query_type is "" when no keyword leads the statement, but first_sql_keyword returns a leading unquoted identifier uppercased (foo bar -> FOO).
The empty-SQL check uses str.strip(), so comment-only SQL passes it and, with read_only off, reports 1 row(s) affected for a no-op.
RunSqlTool.execute tokenizes the same SQL twice (first_sql_keyword and is_read_shaped).
The _cte_reference_ids catch-all logs only the exception type at INFO, too little to diagnose withheld CTE-prefix results.

READ_RESULT_ATTR marks only read frames, so the tool ORs it with its own is_read_shaped; a tool/runner dialect mismatch would show a rows_affected frame as a result table (unreachable on shipped wiring).
RunSqlTool.dialect is an optional, unvalidated, public string not tied to the wrapped runner's dialect; an unknown dialect warns twice per call.
_cte_reference_ids relies on normalize_identifiers rewriting in place and matches nodes by id(); a copying normalization would silently exclude nothing.

report:
## Verdict: APPROVE with notes (findings below the critical threshold and three inconclusive checklist items)

The PR is ready to merge: no finding or checklist failure reaches the critical threshold, every acceptance criterion has a checklist item, and the notes below are worth fixing but block nothing.
Rule applied: rule 6 — findings and checklist FAILs below the threshold, plus INCONCLUSIVE items → APPROVE with notes

## Code Review Findings

### 🟠 Important / Major

1. `changelog.d/324.fixed.md` lines 1-2 say `query_database` "now gets the rows of every read the agent runs", but with `read_only` off some reads still get a row count and lose their rows. Examples: `EXPLAIN …`, `VALUES (1)`, SQLite `PRAGMA table_info(...)`, Postgres `INSERT … RETURNING`, and a read the tokenizer rejects, such as SQLite `SELECT n FROM widgets /* note`. Routing still uses the keyword set `{SELECT, WITH, UNION, INTERSECT, EXCEPT, SHOW}` (`src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py` lines 40-42), and criterion 38 keeps that routing on purpose, so only the note's wording overclaims. (raised by 2/6 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=not-held; evidence: the mechanism is is_read_shaped's keyword set plus the runners' write branch, which a prose fix does not change; git grep —no-index of view-head/scripts and view-head/.github for changelog.d finds only scripts/changelog.py, which assembles CHANGELOG.md text and decides no behavior; a changelog fragment is a published release note -->
- VC-5: FAIL (important) — The release note states that query_database now gets the rows of every read the agent runs, not only of statements that start with the word SELECT. [changelog.d/324.fixed.md:1] [behavior-inert prose cap] <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=not-held; evidence: first-conjunct held (the subject is the release-note sentence "every read the agent runs"; rewording it changes no output, branch or covered set: is_read_shaped's keyword set {SELECT, WITH, UNION, INTERSECT, EXCEPT, SHOW} and the runners' write branch are unchanged by any prose fix, and criterion 38 keeps that routing deliberately); limb-one held (git grep —no-index of view-head/scripts and view-head/.github for changelog.d finds only scripts/changelog.py, which reads fragment bodies to assemble CHANGELOG.md text and decides no program behavior; no agent loads changelog.d as instructions); limb-two not-held (a changelog fragment is a release note published outside the repository) -->

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  changelog.d/324.fixed.md:1-2 says query_database gets the rows of 'every read the agent runs'. In the head view the read/non-read decision is still a first-keyword allowlist: safety/readonly.py:40-42 _READ_SHAPED_KEYWORDS = {SELECT, WITH, UNION, INTERSECT, EXCEPT, SHOW}; is_read_shaped (readonly.py:88-96) is first_sql_keyword in that set, and first_sql_keyword returns '' when the tokenizer raises TokenError (readonly.py:68-71). SqliteRunner._run_sql_blocking (sqlite/sql_runner.py:148-157) executes args.sql, and for anything not read-shaped skips fetch and returns DataFrame({'rows_affected': [cursor.rowcount]}) without READ_RESULT_ATTR. RunSqlTool.execute (tools/run_sql.py:78) then takes the read branch only if is_read_shaped or the READ_RESULT_ATTR mark is set; otherwise it reports 'N row(s) affected' (run_sql.py:171-185) and drops the rows. Counterexamples with read_only=False on SQLite (the runner executes them): `EXPLAIN SELECT 1`, `VALUES (1)`, and `SELECT n FROM widgets /* note` (unterminated comment: sqlglot tokenizer raises TokenError so keyword is '', SQLite runs it) are all reads whose rows are dropped and reported as a row count. So the note's 'every read' overclaims; it is true only for reads whose first keyword is in the set (plus the listed shapes).

  </details>

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (8)

<details><summary>8 items</summary>

1. `docs/internal/mcp-server/tools.md` line 302 says `query_type` is `""` "when no keyword leads the statement", but `first_sql_keyword` returns any leading unquoted identifier, uppercased (`src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py` lines 77-78). The test `test_unquoted_identifier_is_returned` pins `first_sql_keyword("foo bar", "postgres") == "FOO"`. (raised by 1/6 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=held; evidence: the mechanism is first_sql_keyword's VAR branch, which a prose fix does not change; docs/internal is an internal page that no tool or agent loads as instructions, and nothing publishes it -->
2. `src/sqllens/agent/tools/run_sql.py` lines 67-68 decide whether SQL is empty with `args.sql.strip()`, not the tokenizer. So a comment-only statement such as `-- nothing` passes the check, and with `read_only` off it reaches the runner's write branch and reports "1 row(s) affected" for a no-op. Criterion 34 only asks about whitespace, so the behavior is within spec. (raised by 1/6 agents)
3. `src/sqllens/agent/tools/run_sql.py` lines 73-78 tokenize the same SQL twice in one call: `first_sql_keyword` at line 73 and `is_read_shaped` at line 78. The runner and the formatter tokenize it again. The result is correct and the cost is small. (raised by 1/6 agents)
4. `src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py` lines 164-172 (`_cte_reference_ids`): the catch-all logs only the exception's type name, at INFO, and drops its message. When this branch fires, every data query whose CTE name starts with a catalog prefix has its result table withheld, and the log holds too little to diagnose why. (raised by 1/6 agents)
5. `src/sqllens/agent/tools/run_sql.py` lines 75-78: `READ_RESULT_ATTR` marks only the runner's read frames, and the write frame is left unmarked. So the tool cannot tell "the runner chose the write branch" apart from "the runner never marks", and it ORs the mark with its own `is_read_shaped`. If the tool's dialect and the runner's dialect disagree, a `rows_affected` frame is shown as a result table. `build_agent` gives both the same dialect, so the shipped wiring cannot reach this. (raised by 1/6 agents)
6. `src/sqllens/agent/tools/run_sql.py` lines 29-47: `RunSqlTool.dialect` is an optional, unvalidated, public string, and nothing ties it to the dialect of the runner it wraps. If it is omitted, the default `None` classifies across engines, so a `#`-led MySQL read gets a row count. An unknown dialect is caught on every call, not at construction, so its warning is logged twice per call. (raised by 1/6 agents)
7. `src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py` lines 142-172: `_cte_reference_ids` discards the return value of `normalize_identifiers` and matches nodes by `id()` in a separate `find_all` walk. This relies on normalization rewriting the tree in place. If it ever returned a copy, the code would silently exclude nothing (the safe direction), and only the CTE-prefix tests would catch it. (raised by 1/6 agents)
- VC-50: FAIL (suggestion) — transport.md states RunSqlTool.execute writes the result CSV when a read-shaped statement (is_read_shaped under the configured dialect) returns rows; the code also writes it when the frame carries READ_RESULT_ATTR, so the doc condition must match RunSqlTool.execute's branch condition, and the linked tool-scratch-storage.md must describe that classification. [docs/internal/mcp-server/transport.md:123]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  run_sql.py:78 branches on `is_read_shaped(args.sql, self.dialect) or df.attrs.get(READ_RESULT_ATTR)`, with the comment at 75-77 saying a runner-marked frame is reported as a read even when the tool's dialect classifies the statement otherwise. transport.md:123 states the CSV write condition only as 'a read-shaped statement (is_read_shaped under the configured database's dialect)', which omits the READ_RESULT_ATTR arm. The linked tool-scratch-storage.md:7 says the write happens for any statement `is_read_shaped` classifies as read-shaped, 'the same classifier and dialect the runner routes with', and :14 says 'Only statements that are not read-shaped get the row-count summary'. Neither file describes the runner-marked frame path; the only doc mention of READ_RESULT_ATTR is the constant name in read-only-safety.md:124. So a statement the tool's dialect does not classify as read-shaped, but whose frame the runner marked, gets a CSV and rows in the code, which both docs say it does not.

  </details>

</details>

### ℹ️ Informational — Deferred (3)

<details><summary>3 items</summary>

- VC-17: INCONCLUSIVE (suggestion) — read-only-safety.md states sqlglot names the ALTER node exp.Alter at the pinned floor 30.22 (and at 30.26). [docs/internal/database-connectors/read-only-safety.md:33]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  Doc line 33 of docs/internal/database-connectors/read-only-safety.md does make the claim. pyproject.toml:44 pins sqlglot>=30.22,<31. tests/unit/test_safety.py:536-546 (test_alter_parses_to_deny_walk_node) asserts type(parsed) is exp.Alter, but only against whatever sqlglot is installed, so it never pins the 30.22 floor. I read an installed sqlglot 30.26.0 (/Users/the01geek/repos/sqllens/.venv/.../sqlglot/expressions/ddl.py:409), which defines class Alter(Expression), so the 30.26 half is supported. No 30.22 source or lockfile entry was available to read (no *.lock match for sqlglot, only 30.25 and 30.26 venvs found), so I could not confirm the floor half. Not run: installing sqlglot==30.22 and executing the test.

  </details>

- VC-32: INCONCLUSIVE (suggestion) — The docstring asserts comments and opening parentheses are skipped as the dialect's tokenizer skips them, and the first remaining token is returned uppercased when it is a keyword or unquoted identifier, while a string, number, quoted identifier or symbol gives "". [src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py:50]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  readonly.py:60-85 implements the docstring: comments are attached to tokens by the tokenizer (not emitted), L_PAREN tokens are skipped (74-75), a VAR token is returned uppercased (77-78), a keyword token is returned only if its text starts with a letter/underscore and KEYWORDS[text] is the same token type (81-83), anything else (STRING, NUMBER, IDENTIFIER, PARAMETER, symbols) gives "" (84), and no tokens/TokenError gives "" (70-71, 85). In sqlglot's tokens.py no KEYWORDS value maps to STRING/NUMBER/IDENTIFIER/PARAMETER types, so a literal or quoted identifier spelled like a keyword cannot match; COMMANDS (SHOW, EXPLAIN) keep their own token type and match KEYWORDS; VAR_SINGLE_TOKENS is empty in the base tokenizer and in all dialect files, so mysql @var and postgres $1 start with a PARAMETER token and give "". Tests in tests/unit/test_safety_limits.py:175-283 cover several of these. However, the actual tokenizer is a compiled core (TokenizerCore, tokens.py:573-612) whose keyword-scanning code I could not read, and I did not execute any tokenization. So the absolute claim (e.g. whether a multi-word keyword spelled with a newline or double space between words, or a dialect-specific token remap, yields a text that misses the KEYWORDS lookup) is not positively established. Command not run: sqlglot tokenization of the inputs above under each dialect.

  </details>

- VC-35: INCONCLUSIVE (important) — exp.Table stores its schema qualifier under args key "db" and catalog under "catalog", so a qualified table (e.g. main.sqlite_master, pg_catalog.pg_class) is never treated as a CTE reference. [src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py:160]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  The code at src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py:160-161 excludes tables whose args have a truthy 'db' or 'catalog' from the CTE-reference set. This matches the claim's wording. The claim's source of truth is sqlglot's Table.arg_types in sqlglot/expressions.py, and no copy of that file was found: Glob and Grep over the repo, .venv and several site-packages locations found none. The searches of /Users and the other likely locations came up empty or timed out. Missing evidence: sqlglot/expressions.py, class Table, arg_types.

  </details>

</details>

checklist.verify_hint: Trace inputs that are reads but whose first_sql_keyword is outside the read-shaped set or is "": with read_only off on SQLite, `SELECT n FROM widgets /* note` (unterminated comment the tokenizer rejects but SQLite runs), and `EXPLAIN SELECT 1` / `VALUES (1)`; follow them through `is_read_shaped` and the runner's non-read-shaped branch in `SqliteRunner.run_sql` and `RunSqlTool.execute` to see whether rows or a `row(s) affected` message result.
checklist.evidence: changelog.d/324.fixed.md:1-2 says query_database gets the rows of 'every read the agent runs'. In the head view the read/non-read decision is still a first-keyword allowlist: safety/readonly.py:40-42 _READ_SHAPED_KEYWORDS = {SELECT, WITH, UNION, INTERSECT, EXCEPT, SHOW}; is_read_shaped (readonly.py:88-96) is first_sql_keyword in that set, and first_sql_keyword returns '' when the tokenizer raises TokenError (readonly.py:68-71). SqliteRunner._run_sql_blocking (sqlite/sql_runner.py:148-157) executes args.sql, and for anything not read-shaped skips fetch and returns DataFrame({'rows_affected': [cursor.rowcount]}) without READ_RESULT_ATTR. RunSqlTool.execute (tools/run_sql.py:78) then takes the read branch only if is_read_shaped or the READ_RESULT_ATTR mark is set; otherwise it reports 'N row(s) affected' (run_sql.py:171-185) and drops the rows. Counterexamples with read_only=False on SQLite (the runner executes them): `EXPLAIN SELECT 1`, `VALUES (1)`, and `SELECT n FROM widgets /* note` (unterminated comment: sqlglot tokenizer raises TokenError so keyword is '', SQLite runs it) are all reads whose rows are dropped and reported as a row count. So the note's 'every read' overclaims; it is true only for reads whose first keyword is in the set (plus the listed shapes).

checklist.claim: The docstring asserts comments and opening parentheses are skipped as the dialect's tokenizer skips them, and the first remaining token is returned uppercased when it is a keyword or unquoted identifier, while a string, number, quoted identifier or symbol gives "".
checklist.source_excerpt:
The first remaining token is returned,
    uppercased, when it is a keyword or an unquoted identifier; a string,
    number, quoted identifier or symbol gives ``""``, and so does SQL with no
    remaining token (empty, whitespace-only, or only comments and opening
    parentheses).
checklist.verify_against: first_sql_keyword body in readonly.py and sqlglot/tokens.py
checklist.verify_hint: Trace inputs that could falsify it: `SHOW TABLES` under postgres (SHOW may be a COMMAND token whose type differs from KEYWORDS['SHOW']), a keyword whose token type is remapped by a dialect (e.g. a keyword returned as VAR), a mysql `@var` or postgres `$1` first token, and a keyword spelled with a letter case or Unicode letter where `text[:1].isalpha()` differs.
checklist.evidence: readonly.py:60-85 implements the docstring: comments are attached to tokens by the tokenizer (not emitted), L_PAREN tokens are skipped (74-75), a VAR token is returned uppercased (77-78), a keyword token is returned only if its text starts with a letter/underscore and KEYWORDS[text] is the same token type (81-83), anything else (STRING, NUMBER, IDENTIFIER, PARAMETER, symbols) gives "" (84), and no tokens/TokenError gives "" (70-71, 85). In sqlglot's tokens.py no KEYWORDS value maps to STRING/NUMBER/IDENTIFIER/PARAMETER types, so a literal or quoted identifier spelled like a keyword cannot match; COMMANDS (SHOW, EXPLAIN) keep their own token type and match KEYWORDS; VAR_SINGLE_TOKENS is empty in the base tokenizer and in all dialect files, so mysql @var and postgres $1 start with a PARAMETER token and give "". Tests in tests/unit/test_safety_limits.py:175-283 cover several of these. However, the actual tokenizer is a compiled core (TokenizerCore, tokens.py:573-612) whose keyword-scanning code I could not read, and I did not execute any tokenization. So the absolute claim (e.g. whether a multi-word keyword spelled with a newline or double space between words, or a dialect-specific token remap, yields a text that misses the KEYWORDS lookup) is not positively established. Command not run: sqlglot tokenization of the inputs above under each dialect.

checklist.claim: transport.md states RunSqlTool.execute writes the result CSV when a read-shaped statement (is_read_shaped under the configured dialect) returns rows; the code also writes it when the frame carries READ_RESULT_ATTR, so the doc condition must match RunSqlTool.execute's branch condition, and the linked tool-scratch-storage.md must describe that classification.
checklist.source_excerpt: - When a read-shaped statement (`is_read_shaped` under the configured database's dialect, see [tool-scratch-storage.md](../agent/tool-scratch-storage.md)) returns rows, `RunSqlTool.execute` writes the result CSV through `LocalFileSystem.write_file`, an `async` method that calls `mkdir` and `write_text` synchronously.
checklist.verify_hint: Compare the condition at run_sql.py line 78 (`is_read_shaped(...) or df.attrs.get(READ_RESULT_ATTR)`) with the doc sentence, and read docs/internal/agent/tool-scratch-storage.md for its description of when the CSV is written.
checklist.evidence: run_sql.py:78 branches on `is_read_shaped(args.sql, self.dialect) or df.attrs.get(READ_RESULT_ATTR)`, with the comment at 75-77 saying a runner-marked frame is reported as a read even when the tool's dialect classifies the statement otherwise. transport.md:123 states the CSV write condition only as 'a read-shaped statement (is_read_shaped under the configured database's dialect)', which omits the READ_RESULT_ATTR arm. The linked tool-scratch-storage.md:7 says the write happens for any statement `is_read_shaped` classifies as read-shaped, 'the same classifier and dialect the runner routes with', and :14 says 'Only statements that are not read-shaped get the row-count summary'. Neither file describes the runner-marked frame path; the only doc mention of READ_RESULT_ATTR is the constant name in read-only-safety.md:124. So a statement the tool's dialect does not classify as read-shaped, but whose frame the runner marked, gets a CSV and rows in the code, which both docs say it does not.
